description: A junior-level student with a background in competitive programming who is taking the course to formalize their understanding of algorithm analysis and complex data structure implementation.

nodes.title: C++ Foundations: References & Memory
nodes.personalizationRationale: This core node establishes the C++ baseline for a student with strong prior exposure to ensure syntactical consistency with course standards.
nodes.description: Review C++ classes, references, and pointer arithmetic in the context of memory management.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Building on strong prior exposure, this node focuses on the object-oriented design patterns used throughout the textbook.
nodes.title: Object-Oriented Design & Templates
nodes.description: Deep dive into C++ class hierarchies, inheritance, and the use of function templates.

nodes.title: Advanced C++: Move Semantics & RAII
nodes.personalizationRationale: Given the student's strong prior exposure, we provide advanced C++ enrichment on resource management instead of basic scaffolding.
nodes.description: Explore advanced C++ features including R-value references, move semantics, and the RAII idiom for resource management.
Implementation of singly and doubly linked lists, focusing on pointer manipulation.
nodes.title: Arrays & Linked List Implementation
nodes.personalizationRationale: A student with strong prior exposure will focus on the rigorous C++ implementation of these fundamental structures.
This covers essential theoretical foundations that are examined for every student regardless of prior coding experience.
nodes.title: Recursion & Asymptotic Analysis
nodes.description: Introduction to Big-O notation and recursive problem-solving techniques.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Core material required for the midterm, focusing on the interface vs. implementation distinction.
nodes.title: Stacks & Queues ADTs
nodes.description: Abstract Data Types (ADTs) for Stacks and Queues and their implementation using arrays and lists.
Exploration of dynamic arrays (Vectors) and the iterator pattern in C++.
nodes.title: Vectors & Iterators
nodes.personalizationRationale: Standard STL-like patterns are critical for students with strong prior exposure to master for efficient development.
This node fulfills the requirement for sequence-based structures and elementary sorting theory.
nodes.title: Sequences & Bubble Sort
nodes.description: Understanding Sequences and the mechanics of the Bubble Sort algorithm.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Cumulative midterm assessment ensures the student with strong prior exposure meets the specific academic benchmarks of the course.
nodes.title: Midterm Review & Quiz 2
nodes.description: Comprehensive assessment of material from Blocks 1-3, including a review of recursion and Big-O.

nodes.title: General Trees & Traversals
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core syllabus requirement for understanding non-linear data structures.

Properties and implementation of Binary Trees and depth-first searches.

Assessment of hashing strategies, skip lists, and Quiz 3 content.
